meta.title: Task Group A: Schema-enforced AI-first + Scope Constraints (X-to-Demo)
meta.owner_intent: Modify the spec-generation process by evolving the Phase 1/2/3 schemas so outputs are AI-first, minimal, and constrained to 1–3 headline demo items.

context.what_x_to_demo_is: X-to-Demo is an internal generator that produces FeatureSpec, DemoSpec, and CodeSpec artifacts describing a downstream demo app. Do NOT work on any X-to-Demo studio UI concerns.
context.pipeline_shape: Pipeline is exactly 3 phases: feature_spec → demo_spec → code_spec. Keep this unchanged.

global_principles.principle: AI/technical innovation must be the first-class citizen of the proposed demo app.
Constrain demonstrable functionality to 1–3 headline items.
Avoid plumbing by default (auth, billing, observability, etc.) unless explicitly required.
Demo UI must be minimalist and web-browser compatible.
Smartphone-framed browser view ONLY when the proposal indicates a mobile app.
Include an interactive in-app walkthrough spec (auto-start + retriggerable + cancellable).
CodeSpec must remain stack-flexible (constraints, not prescriptive framework choices).

scope.in_scope: Implement Task Group A only: A1, A2, A3 (schema changes). Make only minimal supporting edits needed to keep imports/exports/build healthy.
scope.out_of_scope: Do NOT implement Task Group B (prompt changes), Task Group C (schema-compat deep refactors), pipeline orchestration changes, extra phases, or any new features unrelated to schemas.

files_to_edit.file: Update exports only if required by the repo import graph.

implementation_rules.rule: Follow existing schema coding conventions (Pydantic version, BaseModel style, Field usage, naming).
Schema-enforce headline bounds: all headline capability/demo item lists must be min=1 and max=3.
Prefer strict models (repo-equivalent of extra/forbid) so OpenAI structured outputs remain reliable.
Do not add unrelated acceptance criteria or new product scope. Keep changes schema-focused.

For conditional requirements (tools needed vs not; mobile framing vs not), use unions/oneOf ONLY if the repo’s structured-output schema constraints tolerate it; otherwise encode explicit booleans plus strong field descriptions.
Maintain stack flexibility in CodeSpec; represent tech stack as constraints/compat requirements.

task.title: Phase 1 schema: Force AI-first framing and headline selection

add_required_object.name: tooling_need_assessment
add_required_object.field: May be "not needed" when needs_tools is false.

add_required_array.name: excluded_plumbing
add_required_array.description: Explicit list of common plumbing components that are out-of-scope unless the proposal requires them.

adjust_existing_field.name: acceptance_criteria
adjust_existing_field.requirement: Ensure acceptance criteria are explicitly limited to the 1–3 headline AI capabilities. Prefer a structured criterion object that includes a capability_ref if feasible.

acceptance_checks.check: FeatureSpec schema requires innovation_focus.ai_headline_capabilities with min=1, max=3.
FeatureSpec schema requires excluded_plumbing and discourages plumbing by default via descriptions.
New nested models are strict (repo pattern) and do not allow arbitrary extra fields.

task.title: Phase 2 schema: DemoSpec must be a showcase plan (not a presenter script)

item_model.name: HeadlineDemoItem
item_model.field: Must reference one of the Phase 1 headline AI capabilities.
Describe the model-call moment and what is innovative.

add_required_object.name: smartphone_frame
add_required_object.description: Smartphone frame must be enabled only when is_mobile_like is true; otherwise explicitly disabled. If enforceable via union/oneOf without breaking structured-output schema strictness, implement it.

add_required_object.name: interactive_walkthrough
add_required_object.description: Walkthrough is an in-app interactive UI tour, not a presenter script and not external instructions.

add_required_object.name: tooling_plan_if_needed
add_required_object.description: Must explicitly state either: no tools used, OR tools used with synthetic data and a UI-visible tool-call log. Prefer a discriminated union if feasible.

adjust_existing_field.name: demo_scope
adjust_existing_field.requirement: Ensure consistent with minimalism and excludes plumbing by default.

acceptance_checks.check: DemoSpec schema requires headline_demo_items with min=1, max=3.
DemoSpec schema requires interactive_walkthrough with auto_start_on_launch=true and steps.
DemoSpec schema requires system theme support.

task.title: Phase 3 schema: CodeSpec must include OpenAI integration + tests + walkthrough implementation

add_required_object.name: prompt_pack
add_required_object.description: Initial system/dev/user prompts per headline item.

add_required_object.name: guardrails
add_required_object.description: Basic input filters + refusal policy + short-circuit behavior.

add_optional_object.name: tooling
add_optional_object.description: Only if tools are required. Must include: tool definitions, synthetic data source, and requirement to display tool calls and results in the UI.

add_required_object.name: ui_constraints
add_required_object.field: Must be conditional: smartphone-framed view only when DemoSpec.device_target.is_mobile_like is true.

adjust_existing_object.name: tech_stack
adjust_existing_object.requirement: Keep tech_stack but represent as constraints/compatibility requirements (not prescriptive framework picks). Examples: frontend_constraints, backend_constraints, language_constraints.

acceptance_checks.check: CodeSpec schema requires openai_integration.selected_apis with min=1 and allowed values.
CodeSpec schema requires walkthrough_implementation, testing_strategy, and ui_constraints.
CodeSpec remains stack-flexible (constraints rather than mandated frameworks).

steps.step: Run existing unit tests (or minimal import checks) to ensure schema modules load cleanly.
Generate JSON schema for FeatureSpec/DemoSpec/CodeSpec and confirm required fields and list bounds.
Confirm strictness pattern is preserved (no unintended additional properties in nested models).

reporting_instructions.when_done: Reply with: (1) list of files changed, (2) summary of schema changes per phase, (3) any schema-compat risks or compromises, (4) how to verify locally.
